findings.evidence: launch blocks TERM/INT while spawning the bootstrap and restores only the parent mask. Neither bootstrap nor outer_worker clears the inherited mask. The control worker runs original run.main in that state. Its old blocked mask is restored after original handler installation, so the real self-TERM queued by host-pending-term stays blocked instead of reaching interrupted. Direct IO/auth tasks also keep TERM blocked until a later reset/KILL. host_peer resets only its own role, not the control worker executing R.main.
futureControls: P01 host-pending-term must record the actual original interrupted first refusal and fresh absence
P01 EOF/bootstrap-close still proves no peer exec on missing ACK
Owned IO/auth cleanup must retain actual TERM/KILL outcomes, no assumption of delivery
findings.impact: Named real pending-TERM control cannot establish its intended original predicate. Graceful outer cleanup attempts against the new workers may not be delivered. No actual result was run.
findings.minimumCorrection: In a separately authorized successor, reset the child signal mask only after the owned bootstrap has received the authenticated ACK and before the bound outer_worker role begins, retaining the parent critical-region mask/registration order. Verify the exact previous mask semantics of original R.main and preserve the real pending-TERM injection and intended interrupted refusal; no scripted substitute.
findings.title: Outer workers inherit blocked TERM/INT, defeating the pending-TERM host control

findings.evidence: The two stream records each permit268435456 bytes, so e.g.160MiB stdout plus160MiB stderr passes this local capacity check despite exceeding the original total raw-log256MiB policy. s.bytes is incremented and the refusal is raised before s.file.write(block), dropping the chunk already read from the pipe. The accepted source collector merges product stdout/stderr into one actual log, writes before scanning, and treats256MiB as acceptance threshold, not truncation/disk maximum.
futureControls: Within J10 existing ID, aggregate below/equal/over256MiB with split stdout/stderr, each individually below256MiB
Crossing chunk retained exact; overflow remains failed/inconclusive; no fabricated full hash/EOF
Blocked drain/writer receives unchanged whole clock and ownership controls
findings.impact: Unreviewed per-stream widening and incomplete oversized raw-byte retention in the new outer collector. This does not change immutable scanner.py, but contradicts the claimed inherited evidence policy.
findings.minimumCorrection: Use one aggregate counter for actual stdout+stderr raw acceptance. Preserve the exact bytes already received (including crossing chunk) before marking overflow. Retain/drain actual pending bytes in an owned writer under the same clock while cleanup runs; if EOF or hashing cannot finish, mark them UNKNOWN and refuse acceptance. Never introduce truncation, postdeadline pass or a hard disk-output claim. Remove per-stream reinterpretation from DATA.
findings.title: Outer IO doubles the accepted raw budget and discards the crossing chunk
